Subject: HydraNet discovery — integration & routing follow-up

Thanks again for the demo earlier today, Elena — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of needs we heard
- High-volume chat assistant (user messages peak ~1k req/min) with sub-200ms p50 generation for short replies.
- Sensitive PII in transcripts -> want private deployment / VPC for logs and KMS integration.
- Multi-region presence (US + EU) for latency and compliance.
- Need embeddings+reranker for semantic search over product docs; expect ~10M vectors eventually.

Immediate technical asks you flagged
1) SDK + auth pattern (recommended)
- Server-side SDK (node/python) with short-lived API tokens minted by your auth service via Redwood token-issuing endpoint. Pattern:
  - 1) Backend calls your KMS-protected service -> requests short-lived session token from Redwood (OAuth client creds + CMK proof)
  - 2) Use session token for inference calls; tokens TTL ~15min to limit blast radius.
  - 3) For Private deployments tokens are validated against your IDP (SAML/OIDC) or mutual TLS for on-prem.

2) Model routing + policy configuration
- Suggest two-tier routing policy for POC:
  - latency-first route: routes requests to hosted low-latency instance in nearest region (p50 < 200ms) using smaller model variant (quantized) with fast KV cache.
  - cost-fallback route: if cost threshold or throughput demands increase -> route to dedicated reserved capacity pool (higher throughput, slightly higher tail latency).
  - fallback chain: primary model -> smaller quantized variant -> regional replica -> best-effort CPU-backed variant for non-interactive batch backfill.

Policy knobs we recommend exposing in your UI/API:
- target_p50_ms, max_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd, allowed_model_variants, region_preference_order, enable_prefix_caching.

3) Structured output/tool calling
- Redwood supports function/tool calling with explicit schema enforcement. We recommend: define a strict JSON schema for order extraction, include schema in the call meta; enable "strict_mode" in the route so the runtime will reject outputs that do not conform (returns a structured-error with original tokens). This is what most customers use for deterministic ingestion.

4) Latency & cost estimates with conservative batching assumptions

Proposed next steps
- Marcus will send an architecture note with SDK examples and an auth pattern we recommend (by EOD tomorrow).
- Camila will outline a sample routing + fallback policy (latency-first for prod, cost-aware for bulk ingestion) and an embeddings plan including suggested quantization/replication (by Wed).
- Elena: if you can send your security questionnaire and ETA on the procurement timeline we’ll prepare the Private deployment checklist and a draft SOW.

Attachments: redwood_sdk_quickstart.zip (SDK snippets + example server flow), hydranet_integration_matrix.csv (initial integration checklist).

Thanks — happy to hop on a short technical call if that helps (30m).

Best,
Jasmine Liu

Elena — quick technical note before our Wed call. High level then examples attached.

1) SDK + auth pattern (recommended)- Server-side SDK (node/python) with short-lived API tokens minted by your auth service via Redwood token-issuing endpoint. Pattern:
  - 1) Backend calls your KMS-protected service -> requests short-lived session token from Redwood (OAuth client creds + CMK proof)
  - 2) Use session token for inference calls; tokens TTL ~15min to limit blast radius.
  - 3) For Private deployments tokens are validated against your IDP (SAML/OIDC) or mutual TLS for on-prem.

2) Model routing + policy configuration- Suggest two-tier routing policy for POC:
  - latency-first route: routes requests to hosted low-latency instance in nearest region (p50 < 200ms) using smaller model variant (quantized) with fast KV cache.
  - cost-fallback route: if cost threshold or throughput demands increase -> route to dedicated reserved capacity pool (higher throughput, slightly higher tail latency).
  - fallback chain: primary model -> smaller quantized variant -> regional replica -> best-effort CPU-backed variant for non-interactive batch backfill.

Policy knobs we recommend exposing in your UI/API:
- target_p50_ms, max_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd, allowed_model_variants, region_preference_order, enable_prefix_caching.

3) Structured output/tool calling- Redwood supports function/tool calling with explicit schema enforcement. We recommend: define a strict JSON schema for order extraction, include schema in the call meta; enable "strict_mode" in the route so the runtime will reject outputs that do not conform (returns a structured-error with original tokens). This is what most customers use for deterministic ingestion.

4) Embeddings & reranker suggestion- POC: use managed embeddings with HNSW index (balanced recall/latency). For your 200k initial vectors HNSW with ef_search=64 should be fine. For 10M long-term: partition by namespace + use sharded HNSW with per-shard replicas. Add a lightweight reranker model (small cross-encoder) to rescore top-K (K=50) to maintain quality without large costs.

5) Latency/cost estimates (rough)
- Short reply generation (<=128 tokens) on hosted quantized variant: p50 ~110–160ms, cost ~$0.06 per 1k tokens.
- Reranker step (top50 cross-encoder): add ~45–75ms per query, cost ~$0.12 per 100 queries.
- Bulk embeddings ingestion cost depends on batch throughput — we can provide a CSV-based cost projection (attached).

Attachments: hydranet-maP-arch-diagram.png (deployment sketch), hydranet_integration_matrix.csv (matrix with routes/policies), redwood_sdk_quickstart.zip (examples).

I also added a sample routing JSON config in the attachment with the fallback chain and a canary policy for gradual rollouts. We can walk through it Wed.

Elena — a couple of practical notes from the ops/optimization side ahead of the call: 

- Embeddings/reranker ops: for POC we’ll recommend a single HNSW shard with a replica for failover. Moving to 10M vectors we’ll plan for 8 shards + 2 replicas; we’ll include an estimated storage + query-cost spreadsheet.
- Canary & policy: recommend starting with a 5% canary of traffic on latency-first route for 48 hours, monitor p50/p95 and rollback if p95 > 450ms or error_rate > 0.5%.
- Region routing: set region_preference_order = [us-west-1, us-east-1, eu-west-1] for your initial deployment; ensure KV cache warmup in each region to avoid cold-start p95 spikes.
- Autoscaling suggestion: scale by concurrent sessions (not token rate) for chat to keep tail latency predictable.

I’ll add these notes to the Drive doc and post the canary JSON sample there.

Thanks, looking forward to the Wed 10:30 PT deep-dive.
